findings.highlight: It’s dangerous to make a move
findings.evidenceJa: ここを離れるのは危険
findings.governingReading: Until the event is understood, Shirou judges it dangerous to leave this place.
findings.explanation: The English changes the spatially specific decision to remain into generic caution about acting.

findings.evidenceJa: 慎重な行動は間違いじゃない
findings.governingReading: Rin explicitly tells Shirou that cautious action is not a mistaken choice.
findings.explanation: The English loses her defense against the possibility that remaining is cowardly or wrong.

findings.highlight: wasn’t that the case against Saber as well
findings.evidenceJa: 敗ける筈がなかったのは、セイバーも同じではなかったか
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls that Saber too was someone who should never have lost, yet did.
findings.explanation: The English grammatically makes Saber the opponent in a prior comparison, obscuring the warning analogy.

findings.highlight: I’m making the same mistake again
findings.evidenceJa: 同じ間違いをしたのではないか
findings.governingReading: Shirou fears he may already have repeated his former mistake.
findings.explanation: The English changes retrospective dread into an action currently in progress.

findings.highlight: My retinas are seared by black light
findings.evidenceJa: 網膜が黒い光に麻痺している
findings.governingReading: Black light has paralyzed or overwhelmed Shirou’s retinas like direct sunlight.
findings.explanation: The English implies burning physical damage rather than temporary sensory paralysis.

findings.highlight: My mind, filled with ominous presentiment, is filled with a different kind of uneasiness
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌な予感に翳っていた心中が、別の不安に満たされていく
findings.governingReading: A heart already shadowed by foreboding becomes filled instead with a different anxiety.
findings.explanation: The English produces clumsy repetition and loses the emotional replacement.

findings.highlight: A complete darkness in which I have no sense of direction
findings.evidenceJa: 右も左も、上も下も分からない完全な闇
findings.governingReading: The darkness erases right and left, above and below.
findings.explanation: The English flattens the exhaustive spatial disorientation into generic directionlessness.

findings.highlight: It feels as if I’m swallowed into “nothingness”
findings.evidenceJa: 唐突に、何も“無い”世界に呑み込まれたような、厭な錯覚
findings.governingReading: Shirou suffers an unpleasant illusion that he has suddenly been swallowed by a world in which nothing exists.
findings.explanation: The English removes suddenness, the world, and explicit illusion status.

findings.governingReading: His field of vision has been crushed or obliterated by the black flash.
findings.explanation: The English is nonidiomatic and makes vision sound like a physical object.

findings.highlight: I feel blood on my shoulder
findings.evidenceJa: 肩からはぬるりとした出血
findings.governingReading: Slick blood is flowing from Shirou’s shoulder.
findings.explanation: The English removes active bleeding and tactile viscosity.

findings.evidenceJa: 固い幹に直撃した額は、激しい痛みを呼び起こす
findings.governingReading: His forehead strikes a hard trunk directly, triggering severe pain.
findings.explanation: The mature branch invents an open gash; the alternate branch is malformed and omits the hard-trunk impact.

findings.evidenceJa: 何かの手応えが欲しい
findings.governingReading: Shirou wants tangible resistance or contact as proof that the world remains.
findings.explanation: The English loses the specifically tactile feedback central to the horror transition.

findings.highlight: My eyes just broke down temporarily
findings.evidenceJa: 一時的に視力が飛んだだけ
findings.governingReading: Shirou reassures himself that the flash only knocked out his sight temporarily.
findings.explanation: The English suggests mechanical failure of the eyes and is unnatural.

findings.highlight: I’m only going to pull her leg
findings.governingReading: Blind, Shirou would only hinder or hold Rin back if he rushed after her.
findings.explanation: The English uses an idiom meaning tease or deceive, destroying the tactical judgment.

findings.evidenceJa: あと少しで視界が開ける
findings.governingReading: Shirou insists that his field of vision will open up again shortly.
findings.explanation: The English treats darkness as an external phenomenon that will vanish, weakening the blindness-versus-world contradiction.

findings.highlight: I walk through the darkness, feeling nothing
findings.evidenceJa: 感触のない無を歩いていく
findings.governingReading: Shirou walks through a nothingness that has no tactile presence.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the absence to his sensation and calls the environment darkness, though his sight has already returned.

findings.highlight: I start to get bad ideas
findings.evidenceJa: よくない想像をしてしまう
findings.governingReading: Extreme darkness makes Shirou involuntarily imagine disturbing possibilities.
findings.explanation: The English idiom suggests foolish intentions or plans rather than fearful imaginings.

findings.governingReading: His hypothetical joke is that, without noticing when it happened, he has become trapped in an exitless shadow world.
findings.explanation: The English omits the unnoticed transition that is already becoming reality.

findings.highlight: bitterly laughing at my stupid thought
findings.evidenceJa: あまりのつまらなさに苦笑しながら
findings.governingReading: Shirou moves onward with a wry laugh at how utterly unfunny his supposed joke is.
findings.explanation: The English changes failed humor into intellectual stupidity and weakens his denial mechanism.
